episodes.152417: There were several marine winds gusts ahead of a cold front.
episodes.152423: There were several severe thunderstorm winds gusts ahead of a cold front.
episodes.152425: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a strong cold front.
episodes.152471: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front draped across northern Illinois during the afternoon hours across central and east-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced marginally severe hail and a lighting strike caused a power pole to become engulfed in flames in Appleton.
episodes.152606: Widespread thunderstorms moved across central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening hours of October 23rd.  Some of these storms briefly produced isolated damaging wind gusts and large hail with the strongest storms across south central Indiana.  Several rounds of storms moved over the same areas at times, but no significant flooding impacts were noted other than some minor flooding in areas that easily flood.  One particularly strong storm produced a wall cloud that was seen south of Brownstown where a tornado warning was in place.
episodes.152687: A nearby front and upper air troughs generated periods of heavy rain across Oahu and Kauai. The precipitation caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding. No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.152720: A persistent surge of relatively moist and unstable air north of a stationary front brought heavy rain and flash flooding to portions of south central WI. 4-6 inches of rain fell. Various creeks or low lying areas flooded and resulted in some flooded, washed out, and closed roads.
episodes.152729: A strong upper trough moved across Eastern Oklahoma and East-Central Texas during the morning hours of October 23rd, before progressing east across Southwest Arkansas and North Louisiana during the afternoon. This trough reinforced a strong cold front southeast through the region, with warm, humid air and deepening moisture spreading north into the areas ahead of the front. With the increase in large scale forcing along and ahead of the front and accompanying upper trough, scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed over much of the region, with one of these storms briefly becoming severe during the early afternoon hours over Central Angelina County, where damaging winds downed a few trees and power lines in Downtown Lufkin. These storms diminished during the late afternoon and early evening with the departure of the front, as much cooler air drier air spilled southeast in its wake.
episodes.152751: On the 23rd, another front was set to cross the area, and promised to bring some precipitation followed by much cooler air. As the front crossed the state, scattered showers and thunderstorms popped up mainly in the southern and eastern counties. Some places picked up one to two inches of rain in the twenty four hour period ending at 600 am CST on the 24th. This included Alicia (Lawrence County), Batesville (Independence County), Crystal Valley (Pulaski County), Des Arc (Prairie County), Keo (Lonoke County), and Sheridan (Grant County).
episodes.152790: A deepening surface low migrated across and northeast of Lake Huron during the afternoon. At the same time, a 70 to 90 knot 500 mb speed maximum and mid-level cold core lagged to the southwest, and to the cool side of the trailing cold front. A broken line of thunderstorms accompanied the cold front.
episodes.152792: A deepening surface low migrated across and northeast of Lake Huron during the afternoon. At the same time, a 70 to 90 knot 500 mb speed maximum and mid-level cold core lagged to the southwest, and to the cool side of the trailing cold front. A broken line of thunderstorms accompanied the cold front.
episodes.152818: A line of strong to severe storms tracked across Southeast Michigan on the afternoon of October 23, 2020 ahead of a strong cold front. The storms led to numerous reports of wind damage (trees downed and damage to outbuildings or roofs) and several instances of hail. Tens of thousands of customers lost power across the state due to the storms.
episodes.152820: A thunderstorm near Lexington Harbor produced a wind gust to 36 knots.
episodes.152821: A thunderstorm moving through Lake St. Clair produced a 45 knot wind gust.
episodes.152901: A line of thunderstorms moved through the area in the early morning hours. A 60 mph wind gust was reported in the Granbury area.
episodes.152914: Isolated severe storms resulted in several reports of damaging wind gusts across portions of Eaton, Clinton and Jackson counties.
episodes.152960: A cold front moved from west to east through southern Indiana. Storms associated with the front caused isolated hail and tree damage in multiple counties.
episodes.152961: A cold front moved from west to east through north-central Kentucky. Storms associated with this line damaged a few trees in two Kentucky counties.
episodes.153045: A continuous stream of moisture translated into scattered showers and thunderstorms. Given the already saturated grounds, heavy rainfall resulted in flooding across portions of Palm Beach.
episodes.153123: As a surface low moved northeastward from northern Lake Huron to southwestern Quebec between early afternoon and early evening on October 23rd, the trailing cold front swept eastward and reached north-central and southwestern Ohio by early evening. A squall line developed along the cold front. Ahead of the squall line, discrete thunderstorms, including supercells, occurred. Some of these storms became severe and produced quarter-size hail or damaging wind gusts in northern Ohio. The pre-storm environment exhibited moderate vertical wind shear and DCAPE, respectively, and weak to primarily moderate instability.
episodes.153342: Deepening low pressure and associated cold front moved into the northern Great Lakes. This front interacted with CAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG and 30+ knots of shear to help spark of small areas of thunderstorms. The best instability was centered in northwestern Ohio where a few storms began to produce marginally severe weather.
episodes.153347: As a surface low moved northeastward from northern Lake Huron to southwestern Quebec between early afternoon and early evening on October 23rd, the trailing cold front swept eastward and reached central Lake Erie and north-central Ohio by early evening. A squall line developed along the cold front, while discrete thunderstorms occurred ahead of the squall line. These storms produced strong to severe wind gusts along portions of the Lake Erie shore in northwest, north-central, and northeast Ohio. The pre-storm environment exhibited moderate vertical wind shear and DCAPE, respectively, and weak to moderate instability.
episodes.153374: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on October 23, a few of which became strong to severe. One report of large hail was received.
episodes.153582: A strong cold front moved through the Mid-South during the late afternoon and early evening hours on October 23rd. The front interacted with some marginal instability and a severe storm developed over Carroll County in West Tennessee.
episodes.153692: A strong cold front approached the area subsequent to record heat across western New York. A pre-frontal trough ignited thunderstorms upstream from lower Michigan through northern Ohio. Thunderstorms overall diminished as they moved toward the area late in the evening. Though not impressive in terms of reflectivity and lightning produced, an isolated cell moving toward shore near Buffalo and produced a 62 mph wind gust. Stronger environmental winds from the large scale were likely funneled down the lake and brought to the surface due to the weak convection. An additional later report of some damage at a marina came from the Lake Ontario shoreline as convection moved farther inland in Wilson.
episodes.153899: Low pressure lifted across northern lower Michigan early in the morning of the 23rd. Very heavy rain fell just in advance of this low, late on the 22nd and early on the 23rd. 24 hour rainfall totals were 5.00 in Suttons Bay, 4.98 in Lake Ann, and 4.73 in Gaylord. Following a period of relatively dry weather, most flooding issues were minor. However, more significant road flooding occurred in and near Traverse City. In addition, gusty northwest winds in the wake of the low contributed to lakeshore flooding along the Lake Michigan coast on the 23rd.

events.narrative: A lightning strike caused a power pole to become engulfed in flames on Appleview and Fuji Drive in Appleton.  The power pole and attached light were damaged due to the fire and had to be replaced.
Four to six inches of rain led to some minor road flooding between La Valle and Reedsburg. A section of Birchwood Rd. was washed out and closed on the west side of Lake Delton.

Spring Creek at Lodi reached major flood stage, cresting around 7.6 feet the morning of October 23rd. Floodwaters affect Goeres Park including the pool, and water approaches the Public Works garage, and Habermann park including the baseball diamond.

Road flooding occurred in a number of places in the Traverse City area. Logans Landing along the Boardman River saw the parking lot flood. Eleventh St and Division St saw flooding, as did West Front St and Madison Dr. Flooding also occurred in the Three Mile Rd area, near Mitchel Creek.

Flash flooding of various roads in the far northern portion of Iowa County after 4-5 inches of rain. This included, but not limited to, the intersection of highway 133 and Leaches Crossing Rd., portions of Clyde St. in Avoca, and portions of Coon Rock Rd. near Coon Rock.
A trained spotter measured a 60 mph wind gust in the Granbury area.

Off-duty NWS employee reported ponding of water on Florida Turnpike near mile marker 84 due to training showers over the area during the last several hours. Additional reports from the public via social media of lakes are overflowing, street sewers are backing up, and cars having issues getting through the street in the Valencia Cove neighborhood of Boynton Beach, Florida. Rain gauge measurements in the area range from 1.5-4 inches.
Two non-life threatening injuries after lightning struck an asphalt roller. The driver and a nearby worker were checked out by first responders and released.
